newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ord Minnett's NZ growth indicator falls in July.
newsitem.headline: Ord Minnett's NZ growth indicator falls in July.

text.p: Ord Minnett's New Zealand growth indicator nudged lower in July, cementing in the large falls in May and June, economist Rodney Dickens said on Thursday.
The indicator fell to 103.9 from 104.1 in June and 108.4 in July 1995.
The indicator continues to point to economic growth falling to zero year-on-year for the rest of this year, he said.
The persistence of high bank bill yields around 10 percent meant tight conditions would contiune to offset most, if not all, the impact of the July tax cuts.

Monetary conditions had eased slightly with the fall in bond yields in the last couple of months, encouraging some mortgage rates to fall but mortgages were still well above where they were late last year.
"It will take a larger fall in mortgage interest rates to restimulate the sickening housing market," Dickens said.
He said inflation concerns were likely to dissipate as evidence of the slowing economy accumulated and there should be a more generalised fall in interest rates.
